source.title: Gradient Descent Quantizes ReLU Network Features
source.authors: Hartmut Maennel; O. Bousquet; S. Gelly

record.file_problem: Full text supplied, including appendices and figure captions.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether an idealized gradient descent process and its greedy simulation yield generalizing networks, using a modified training procedure and MNIST test accuracy rather than the original claim’s random-label comparison.
record.gate_note: Reports MNIST test-accuracy comparisons between normal full-network training and greedy training that simulates the idealized model. It also reports qualitative toy-data behavior. The cited Zhang et al. random-label findings are prior work and are not rows. Figure 1 provides no recoverable numeric accuracies in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: Figure 1 measures MNIST test accuracy across widths in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks trained to convergence without explicit regularization; Figure 3 separately measures the width needed for perfect training accuracy. These experiments bear on V2, although the supplied text does not reveal the test-accuracy trends beyond that width.
record.authors_conclusion: The record largely captures the conclusion, but overstates the proof's completeness: the authors argue that infinitesimal-initialization, infinitesimal-step gradient descent selects finitely many simple functions independent of network size, with the final proof steps explicitly informal. Approximation guarantees for restricted smooth distributions remain conjectural. Greedy simulations generalize but sometimes perform worse than ordinary initialization; ensembles appear closer.
record.recipe_differences: One-hidden-layer ReLU networks trained with full-batch gradient descent; experiments compare ordinary training with a greedy neuron-addition algorithm intended to simulate infinitesimal initialization. The study's theory takes infinitesimal initialization and learning rate.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization magnitude has a large effect on the final function. On MNIST, the gap between normal full-network training and greedy training is clear for smaller training sets and much smaller when the number of examples is large. Toy-data behavior also differs between small and large initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Ordinary and greedy training achieve comparable MNIST test performance with many examples, with a gap at smaller sample sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The greedy simulation's agreement with ordinary training depends on training-set size.

fits_no_version.finding: Ordinary and greedy training require similarly small numbers of neurons for perfect MNIST training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The procedures have similar neuron requirements for fitting natural MNIST labels.

record.problems: MNIST test-accuracy results are presented in a figure with no numeric values in the supplied text. The greedy training algorithm is a simulation of the idealized model, not the same training recipe as ordinary gradient descent. The authors say the idealized model does not capture all properties of gradient descent, and the remaining proof comparison relies on an informal continuity argument for stratified differential equations.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported quantitative outcomes could be extracted from Figures 1–3 because the supplied text contains captions but no plotted values. The qualitative comparisons stated in Section 7.3.2 are represented in the figure-only rows.

untested.parts: No original random-label versus natural-label experiment; the coexistence finding is cited.
No downsampled CIFAR-10 experiment. The greedy procedure does not establish the corresponding widening effect under ordinary full-network training.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizer comparison.
No batch-size comparison under controlled epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison of generalization measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.

record.verdict_notes: No V2 verdict is justified because neither the supplied figure captions nor the prose states the direction of test-accuracy change beyond interpolation. Unavailable figure values and omitted figure outcomes are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not duplicated in missing. Failure of a distribution-independent guarantee does not challenge any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fitting random labels or compare random-label test accuracy with natural-label test accuracy; the Zhang et al. result is cited prior work.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold with test error for the stated one-hidden-layer MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10 setting.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-measure comparison.
